proof.text: Fix a compactification c. The base S is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. We use Noetherian induction on its closed subsets, rather than induction on its numerical dimension: prove the conclusion after base change to every reduced closed subscheme E of S, using the conclusion for proper closed subsets of E. Such E is affine of finite type over Z: on rings it is A/I. It is Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma. The smooth relative-dimension permanence lemma gives a smooth relative-dimension-one morphism X_E to E; affineness follows directly by tensoring its affine coordinate algebra with A/I, and separatedness is preserved by base change. These morphisms are of finite presentation, since smoothness gives local finite presentation and qcqs permanence gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Base change and exact inverse image identify the restriction of the original cohomology sheaves with those of this new compact-support object, whose input is again constant by the constant-pullback lemma. The minimal-closed-subset lemma licenses the induction, and the empty closed subset is the immediate base case.

For a nonempty induction base E, choose a generic point eta of an irreducible component. Apply the good-curves diagram to X_E to E. All schemes in this diagram are Noetherian and qcqs: U is an open of the Noetherian affine E, V is finite over U, T_i is finite etale over V, and the remaining schemes are of finite type over these. By shrinking U to an affine neighbourhood of eta and base changing the whole diagram, we may take U affine; all the displayed properties persist. Let a:X_V to V. By compact-support base change, constant pullback, and exactness of inverse image, the pullback to V of each cohomology sheaf on U is the cohomology of Ra_! constant M. Since V to U is surjective, the surjective-pullback constructibility criterion reduces constructibility on U to constructibility on V.

Write Z=(X_V minus W)_red. Every nonempty fibre of X_V to V has dimension one; empty fibres are allowed. The open W is dense in every fibre. Consequently the closed complement has dimension at most zero in each fibre: a dimension-one component cannot be contained in the complement. Explicitly, a chain of two distinct irreducible closed subsets in that complement would have its larger member contained in an irreducible component of the fibre; if this containment were strict it would give a chain of length two in the dimension-one fibre. The larger member must therefore be a whole component, contrary to density of W. There are no such chains, so the complement has dimension at most zero. By the finite-type dimension-zero lemma these fibres are finite discrete spaces. Thus Z to V is quasi-finite by the definition (finite type and isolated fibre points). It is separated and of finite presentation, since it is a closed subscheme of the Noetherian separated finite-type X_V. The constant finite module sheaf on Z is constructible using the one-stratum partition. The quasi-finite shriek lemma makes its compact-support cohomology constructible. Apply the open-closed compact-support triangle to W in X_V. Its long exact sequence gives the short exact sequence 0 to coker(H^(q-1)(RZ_!) to H^q(RW_!)) to H^q(Ra_! constant M) to ker(H^q(RZ_!) to H^(q+1)(RW_!)) to 0. The Serre theorem therefore reduces the assertion to compact support on W.

Put i:nu inverse W to W. This is a closed immersion with empty open complement, since it is a thickening. Apply the cited open-closed compact-support triangle to W to V with this closed complement and K=constant M: its first term is compact support on the empty scheme, hence zero, so its middle-to-last map identifies R(W to V)_! constant M with R(nu inverse W to V)_! i inverse constant M. Constant pullback identifies this last input with constant M. This three-line consequence replaces a separate thickening-invariance lemma. Put Ybar=coproduct_i Ybar_i and Zprime=(Ybar minus j(nu inverse W))_red. The inverse image of W is dense in each fibre of Y_i to T_i; since Y_i is open in a smooth geometrically connected fibre of Ybar_i, it is dense in that fibre as well (apply the smooth-connected generic-geometry lemma over the spectrum of its residue field, an integral normal base whose generic point is its only point, to conclude the fibre is integral; every nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense). In an integral fibre of dimension at most one, a proper closed subset has dimension at most zero: a positive-dimensional irreducible closed subset would have to be the whole fibre, by the chain definition of dimension. Hence each closed complement in a Ybar_i fibre has dimension at most zero, and in dimension zero it is empty. For v in V, the etale-fibre discrete-separable-points lemma identifies the fibre of each T_i to V as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of kappa(v). This union is finite: T_i to V is finite, hence its fibre is affine and quasi-compact, and the singleton open cover of this discrete fibre has a finite subcover. The fibre of Zprime is the corresponding finite disjoint union of the zero-dimensional closed complements in the Ybar_i fibres. The dimension-zero lemma makes this finite and discrete. Since Zprime is a closed subscheme of the Noetherian separated finite-type Ybar, the finite-type-Noetherian-finite-presentation lemma gives finite presentation on affine charts; the definition of quasi-finite then applies. Its constant finite module sheaf is constructible by the one-stratum partition, so the quasi-finite shriek lemma gives constructible cohomology for D=R(Zprime to V)_! constant M. Write A=R(nu inverse W to V)_! constant M and B=R(Ybar to V)_! constant M. The open-closed triangle is A to B to D to A[1]. Its long exact sequence gives 0 to coker(H^(q-1)(B) to H^(q-1)(D)) to H^q(A) to ker(H^q(B) to H^q(D)) to 0. Thus constructibility of B and D implies that of A by the Serre theorem, and it suffices to prove constructibility of B.

For each i let b_i:Ybar_i to T_i and t_i:T_i to V. Properness allows the compactification (identity,b_i), so Rb_i,! is Rb_i,* (extension by zero for the identity is the identity, by its definition). The proper-smooth-curves finite-module lemma gives constructible cohomology for Rb_i,* constant M; it applies without an invertibility assumption on M, because Lambda and M are finite. Since t_i is finite etale, the quasi-finite shriek constructibility lemma applies to this bounded-below complex. Composition identifies Rt_i,! Rb_i,! with R(t_i b_i)_! and hence gives constructible cohomology for every summand. To assemble the finite disjoint union, successively use the relative Mayer-Vietoris triangle with U a union of previous components and V the next component. Their intersection is empty, whose compact-support object is zero, so the triangle gives the finite direct sum of the summands. The Serre theorem closes constructible sheaves under finite sums (each binary sum is a split extension); the empty family gives zero. Independence of compactification permits every comparison just made for the original chosen candidates.

Steps 2 to 5 prove constructibility on the nonempty open U of E for every degree. Let Eprime=(E minus U)_red. It is a proper closed subset of E, so the induction hypothesis applies there. Base change, constant pullback, and exactness of inverse image identify the restriction to Eprime of each cohomology sheaf with the constructible sheaf given by induction. For each fixed degree, take the finite constructible immersed stratification on U and the one on Eprime. Their composite immersions into E give a finite constructible immersed stratification of E: subsets locally closed in an open or closed subset are locally closed in E, and constructible subsets remain constructible because these immersions are quasi-compact on the Noetherian scheme E. On each resulting stratum the inverse image is the same finite locally constant sheaf as before. This proves constructibility directly from its definition and completes Noetherian induction. This yields constructibility on S_red. If S has nilpotents, apply compact-support base change to the surjection S_red to S and use exact inverse image and constant pullback to identify the pullbacks of the original cohomology sheaves with those just proved constructible. The surjective-pullback criterion then gives constructibility on S itself; it requires only qcqs, not flatness or etaleness of this reduction map. Finally use compactification independence to obtain the assertion for every compactification c.

title: Constant finite coefficients on affine smooth relative curves
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For any separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$ consists of a quasi-compact open immersion $j$ and a proper morphism $p$ with $h=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; write $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A$ is a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra. Let $h:X\to S$ be a separated affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; let $M$ be a finite $\Lambda$-module and $\underline M$ the constant sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-constructible-locally-constant], placed in degree zero. Then $\mathcal H^q(Rh_!^c\underline M)$ is constructible for every integer $q$ and every compactification $c$ of $h$.
